HEART DISEASE PREDICTION USING MACHINE LEARNING AND 
DEEP LEARNING TECHNIQUES 
P. Abhinaya 
B. Pujitha 
B22IT082 
B22IT122 
Email: b22it080@kitsw.ac.in 
Email: b22it122@kitsw.ac.in 
 
K. Nandhu 
K. Hrushikesh 
B22IT091 
B22IT090 
Email: b22it091@kitsw.ac.in 
Email: b22it090@kitsw.ac.in 
 
Abstract: 
 This study aims to improve the accuracy of heart 
disease prediction by developing and combining 
multiple machine learning models. Individual models 
such as Gradient Boosting, Restricted Boltzmann 
Machine (RBM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), 
Autoencoder with Classifier, and Neural Networks are 
first evaluated using a heart disease dataset. The top 
three models with the best prediction accuracy and 
lowest error rates are then combined to create hybrid 
models that utilize the strengths of each technique. 
These hybrid models are tested to determine whether 
they perform better than the individual models. The 
study also focuses on improving data quality through 
feature engineering and sensitivity analysis to 
understand the impact of different parameters on 
model performance. The final results can support real-
time clinical decision-making for effective heart 
disease prevention and treatment 
Keywords: Heart Disease Prediction, Machine     
Learning, Deep Learning, Neural networks, Boosting, 
Multilayer perceptron. 
. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Heart diseases are among the topmost medical issues 
facing countless individuals globally. The condition 
leads to numerous fatalities annually due to untimely 
diagnosis and a lack of predictive technologies. The 
problem is further compounded by lifestyle factors, 
stress, and 
unhealthy 
practices, 
which 
make 
individuals at higher risk of contracting cardiovascular 
diseases. 
 
The traditional method used to diagnose heart 
conditions involves performing clinical tests such as 
ECG, blood pressure analysis, lipid profile, and 
knowledge from physicians. While these techniques 
are highly reliable, they are cumbersome, costly, and 
require human interpretation to make any significant 
progress. Early prediction is therefore challenging 
 
 
using these procedures because of their drawbacks. 
There is an increasing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
and Machine Learning (ML) technologies in many 
industries, including the medical sector. Machine 
learning models are equipped with skills to analyze 
enormous amounts of data and identify complex patterns 
within them that are difficult for humans to detect. Such 
models may assist physicians in making faster and more 
accurate predictions. 
This research involves applying multiple machine 
learning algorithms and artificial intelligence models to 
predict heart conditions. Some of these models include 
but are not limited to Logistic Regression, Random 
Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and neural 
networks. 
 
II. LITERATURE REVIEW 
 
A. Traditional Methods for Predicting Heart Disease 
 
Research on automated heart disease prediction has 
evolved from traditional statistical methods to advanced 
machine learning and deep learning techniques. Classical 
models such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, 
SVM, and KNN provide interpretable results but often 
struggle with complex medical data, while ensemble 
methods like Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, and 
AdaBoost achieve better accuracy and robustness. Deep 
learning models such as MLP, FNN, LSTM, and GRU 
further improve prediction by learning complex feature 
relationships and temporal patterns. Recent studies show 
that hybrid models combining boosting algorithms with 
deep learning techniques provide the best performance for 
accurate and reliable heart disease prediction. These 
models enhance early disease detection, reduce prediction 
errors, and support clinical decision-making. They also 
improve the efficiency of healthcare systems by enabling 
faster and more accurate diagnosis of heart disease. 
.

2 
 
B. Prediction Models Based on Machine Learning 
With the development of machine learning models, there 
has been tremendous progress made with heart disease 
prediction models. Machine learning models can be 
trained using massive amounts of data and do not require 
any explicit coding. 
 
There are various algorithms that are used extensively in 
the context of heart disease prediction. The Logistic 
Regression model is popularly used in solving binary 
classification problems and gives decent performance. 
The Support Vector Machine is useful when dealing 
with higher dimensions and optimizing the hyperplane. 
 
Another robust algorithm that uses decision tree 
ensembles to make predictions is called Random Forest. 
Other ensemble techniques such as AdaBoost and 
XGBoost can also give improved performance through 
model aggregation. 
 
Feature selection and preprocessing are some key 
techniques that help in enhancing the accuracy of 
machine learning models. With proper feature selection 
and eliminating noise, better accuracy can be achieved. 
While the use of a single machine learning model can 
yield decent results, there are cases where this approach 
fails. Hence, the need arises for multiple models. 
 
C. Deep Learning and Hybrid Models 
The use of deep learning models in prediction 
models has led to increased accuracy in these 
models. Neural network models have been 
found to capture the intricate relationships 
among input variables and hence their 
suitability in applications involving health care. 
Models such as ANN, MLP, LSTM, and GRU 
have been applied in predicting heart disease 
problems. The models are able to learn feature 
representations automatically, thus leading to 
high accuracy levels. 
Hybrid approaches have also performed better 
in predictive tasks than standalone machine 
learning and deep learning models. Hybrid 
models make use of two different algorithms in 
one system. 
They utilize the benefits of individual 
algorithms and mitigate their weaknesses by 
combining them. For instance, the use of LSTM 
and boosting models such as XGBoost 
increases the accuracy levels. 
 
D. Importance of Data Analytics in the 
Health Care Sector 
 
In today’s health care sector, data analytics has 
become extremely important due to its 
applications in healthcare systems. The use of 
medical big data has allowed scientists to 
devise predictive models that can be used for 
diagnostic purposes and treatment. 
 
Machine learning techniques allow scientists to 
draw valuable information from patient 
records. This can then be used for risk 
detection, and early interventions can be taken 
accordingly. 
 
There are many data preprocessing techniques 
available that include normalization, missing 
value handling, and feature scaling, which are 
very 
important 
for 
enhancing 
model 
performance. 
III. PROPOSED MODEL 
 
A. Proposed Model for Heart Disease Prediction 
 
In this regard, the suggested system will be built on a 
machine learning technique, which uses data of a patient 
for predicting chances of having heart diseases. For 
instance, inputs include some clinical parameters like 
the age of patients, cholesterol level, heart rate, blood 
pressure, and other related variables. 
 
Data pre-processing involves handling missing values as 
well as normalizing the data to make sure that data set is 
clean. It is followed by feature engineering stage, where 
a feature engineering technique is employed to make 
sure that the right features are selected. 
 
The Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) is one of the 
techniques, which can be applied in extracting some 
hidden patterns within the data. 
Finally, data passes to the classification layer, where a 
few machine learning algorithms are applied to classify 
whether the patient has heart diseases or not. These 
include logistic regression, random forest, and support 
vector machine (SVM). 
 
B. Approach to Hybrid Model 
 
In order to enhance the accuracy of predictions, a hybrid 
model approach is suggested that uses both machine 
learning and deep learning. Algorithms like LSTM, 
FNN, RBM, and XGBoost will be used in the 
development of this model. 
 
LSTM can identify sequential patterns in the data, 
whereas XGBoost helps in boosting the accuracy of 
classifications. Combining these two models will ensure 
higher accuracy. 
 
Errors and generalization will be minimized using a 
hybrid model. False negatives and false positives can 
also be minimized using these approaches. Additionally, 
the hybrid model can support more reliable and efficient 
real-time 
heart 
disease 
prediction 
for 
clinical 
applications.

1 
 
IV. EXPERIMENTAL SETUP 
The experiment has been formulated with an objective 
to assess the performance of different machine learning 
and deep learning algorithms in predicting heart diseases 
based on medical data. This part provides information 
on the dataset used, pre-processing, architecture of the 
model, training, and testing. 
 
A. Description of the Dataset 
 
The dataset utilized for this research work comprises 
structured clinical datasets acquired from publicly 
accessible medical databases. The dataset involves 
several patient records having characteristics related to 
the diagnosis of heart disease. 
 
The main features of the dataset are the age, gender, 
chest pain type, resting blood pressure, serum 
cholesterol, 
fasting 
blood 
sugar, 
resting 
electrocardiographic (ECG) test result, maximum heart 
rate obtained, exercise-induced angina, and many more. 
 
The dataset contains categorical and numeric attributes. 
The target attribute is an indicator of whether the 
patients have any heart disease or not. 
 
B. Data Preprocessing 
 
Data preprocessing is important for enhancing the 
performance and efficacy of the prediction models. 
Inconsistencies, missing data, and differences in scale 
among others may affect the accuracy of predictions. 
 
At the first step, missing values are treated appropriately 
through techniques such as using the mean or mode of a 
variable as an imputation method, depending on whether 
it is a categorical or numerical feature. Any duplicate 
values are eliminated. 
 
In case of categorical variables like chest pain type and 
ECG, label or one-hot encoding is used to convert 
categorical features to numeric ones. This enhances the 
interpretability by machine learning algorithms. 
 
Features are also scaled through appropriate methods 
such as Min-Max scaling or standardization, making 
them 
more 
comparable 
and 
improving 
their 
interpretation. 
 
The data is finally split into training and test sets, 
commonly with an 80% training and 20% testing ratio. 
 
C. Feature Engineering 
 
Feature engineering is employed to improve the quality 
of input data and the performance of the predictive 
models. Some of the approaches employed in this 
project include feature selection and transformation. 
 
Correlation analysis is used to find out the most 
important features that contribute to predicting heart 
disease. Unrelated features are filtered out, and highly 
correlated features are removed. 
 
Moreover, sophisticated algorithms such as Restricted 
Boltzmann Machine (RBM) can be employed to extract 
latent representations of the data. 
 
D. Model Configuration and Training 
 
Numerous machine learning and deep learning models 
have been trained on the dataset. 
 
Restricted Boltzman Machine,AdaBoost, and XGBoost 
are some of the machine learning models employed in 
the study. These models were chosen because they have 
proven to work effectively in classification problems. 
 
ANN and LSTM neural networks are also used for 
prediction. The Artificial Neural Network algorithm is 
made up of numerous hidden layers, each of which uses 
an activation function such as ReLU and Sigmoid. 
 
LSTM, on the other hand, captures long-term 
dependencies within the dataset despite its structured 
nature. 
 
Learning rate, the number of trees, tree depth, and 
hidden layers are tuned. 
 
E. Design of the Hybrid Model 
 
To further improve prediction accuracy, we design a 
hybrid model that combines deep learning and machine 
learning approaches. Specifically, our hybrid model 
consists of combining the power of LSTM with that of 
XGBoost. 
 
In our model, we use LSTM for feature extraction and 
apply the XGBoost classifier to do final classification. 
 
F. Performance Metrics 
 
The models are assessed based on various performance 
metrics to evaluate their performance comprehensively. 
 
Accuracy represents the performance of the model in 
terms of overall correctness of predictions. In addition 
to accuracy, precision and recall are used to measure 
how well the model predicts positive and negative cases. 
 
F1-score is a metric that balances between precision and 
recall of the model. ROC curve and AUC values can be 
calculated to measure classification performance. 
 
Confusion matrices provide an overview of model 
performance by illustrating TP, TN, FP, and FN values 
of the model. 
 
G. Experimental Setup

1 
 
Experiments are conducted using Python programming 
language, including libraries such as Scikit-learn, 
TensorFlow, and Keras. 
 
Our model has been developed in a typical computing 
environment with adequate computing power. 
 
V. Results and Discussion 
 
In this part, the performance evaluation of different 
types of machine learning and deep learning algorithms 
employed in heart disease prediction is discussed. The 
findings of this analysis are discussed in light of the 
evaluation metrics and comparisons to determine the 
most suitable model. 
 
A. Performance Evaluation of Models 
 
All machine learning algorithms and deep learning 
algorithms developed for this study were tested based on 
the test dataset. 
The findings suggest that conventional machine learning 
algorithms yield stable results, whereas deep learning 
algorithms exhibit better performance owing to their 
efficiency in capturing complex relationships between 
input variables. 
 
It is observed that among all developed models, Random 
Forest and XGBoost worked efficiently owing to their 
ensembling nature; however, deep learning models, i.e., 
ANN and LSTM, delivered better prediction accuracy. 
 
Fig no 1.1: Figure Depicting Evaluation Metrics of 
single models .  
Table 1 shows the performance comparison of various 
machine learning and deep learning models. It is 
observed that LSTM achieves the highest accuracy of 
0.87, followed by FNN and ensemble-based methods 
such as Random Forest and XGBoost. These results 
indicate that deep learning models are more effective in 
capturing complex patterns in the dataset. 
 
B. Accuracy and Metric Analysis 
 
The accuracy of the models is measured based on 
precision, recall, and the F1-score. 
Logistic regression has moderate accuracy and acts as a 
baseline 
for 
comparison. 
SVM 
has 
consistent 
performance, while random forest and XGBoost have 
better results due to their ability to minimize overfitting 
through various decision trees and gradient boosting 
technique. ANN is better than classical methods due to 
its ability to detect complex interactions between 
features. Finally, LSTM outperforms other algorithms in 
accuracy, demonstrating the ability to learn complicated 
patterns. 
 
The F1-score values prove that all models provide a 
good balance between precision and recall and minimize 
false positives and false negatives. 
 
 
Fig no 1.2: Figure Depicting Evaluation Metrics of 
Hybrid models .  
As shown in Figure 1, deep learning models such as 
LSTM and FNN achieve higher accuracy compared to 
traditional machine learning models. The hybrid model 
further 
improves 
performance, 
indicating 
that 
combining multiple techniques enhances prediction 
capability. 
C. Confusion Matrix Analysis 
 
Confusion matrices are utilized to assess the accuracy of 
the models. 
The proposed models exhibit high accuracy regarding 
true positives and negatives, which indicate the ability 
to classify the disease and absence correctly. 
Additionally, the number of false positives and false 
negatives is relatively low, which plays an essential role 
in medical diagnostics. 
 
It is crucial to minimize false negatives in heart disease 
prediction because neglecting a positive result may lead 
to severe health outcomes. 
 
D. ROC Curve and AUC Analysis 
The Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve 
analyzes the performance of a classifier at various 
threshold settings. 
 
The Area Under the Curve (AUC) results of the models 
show high classification performance levels. Advanced 
models like XGBoost and LSTM perform better than 
traditional classifiers as they have high AUC results, 
indicating their classification prowess. 
The results from the ROC analysis suggest that the

1 
 
advanced classifiers are superior compared to the 
traditional ones in terms of predictive power. 
E. Hybrid Model Performance 
 
From the analysis, the hybrid model made up of LSTM 
and XGBoost performs better than the other models in 
terms of predictive accuracy. 
This is because the hybrid model utilizes the feature 
extraction capabilities of LSTM coupled with the 
classification prowess of XGBoost to minimize errors in 
classification. 
 
Figno1.3:Figure depicting performance comparison 
of hybrid models.  
Among all combinations, the LSTM + XGBoost model 
achieves the highest accuracy of 0.81, along with better 
precision and recall values. This demonstrates that 
combining deep learning with boosting techniques 
significantly 
improves 
prediction 
performance 
compared to other hybrid approaches. 
 
F. Discussion 
Some of the key findings observed from the experiments 
are that machine learning models provide strong baseline 
performance for heart disease prediction, while deep 
learning models outperform traditional approaches by 
effectively learning complex patterns and relationships 
within medical data. Feature engineering significantly 
improves model accuracy by selecting and transforming 
important attributes, and hybrid models achieve the best 
results by combining the strengths of multiple algorithms. 
However, the overall performance of the models depends 
heavily on factors such as dataset size, feature quality, and 
preprocessing techniques, as insufficient or poor-quality 
data can reduce the generalization capability of deep 
learning models. The proposed system demonstrates high 
efficiency, reliability, and predictive capability, making it 
suitable for supporting early diagnosis and real-time 
clinical decision-making in heart disease detection. 
Furthermore, the system helps healthcare professionals 
make faster and more accurate treatment decisions, 
improving overall patient care outcomes. 
 
Fig no 1.4: Figure depicting Acurracies of 
Individual models 
 
Fig no 1.5: Depicting Hybrid model accuracy 
VI. CONCLUSION 
This analysis evaluated both single and hybrid machine 
learning models for heart disease prediction using 
performance metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, 
F1-Score, and AUC. Among the individual models, Long 
Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Feedforward Neural 
Network (FNN), and Restricted Boltzmann Machine 
(RBM) showed better performance than models like 
XGBoost, CatBoost, MLP, and GRU. Based on these 
results, hybrid models were created by combining the best-
performing models. Among all hybrid models, the LSTM 
+ XGBoost model achieved the best results with high 
accuracy (0.81), precision (0.83), recall (0.82), and F1-
score (0.82). Its superior performance is due to the 
effective combination of deep learning and boosting 
techniques, which improves prediction accuracy and 
reduces errors. Compared to other hybrid models such as 
RBM + FNN, XGBoost + RBM, and LSTM + FNN, the 
LSTM + XGBoost model performed the best, showing that 
hybrid approaches are more effective for heart disease 
prediction. 
 
VII. Future Scope 
Despite the success of the proposed system in yielding 
positive results, there are some directions for future 
research and development. 
 
For instance, the future development of this model could 
involve the use of extensive and heterogeneous real-
world datasets, which will increase the robustness and 
flexibility of the model. Furthermore, by adding,

1 
 
genetics, and medical history will make the model even 
more accurate. 
 
Another area for improvement is to use IoT devices and 
wearable technology, which will enable real-time data 
acquisition, thus allowing us to perform real-time 
prediction of patients' health condition. 
 
Using state-of-the-art machine learning approaches, like 
CNNs or transformers, can result in better outcomes. 
The use of explainable artificial intelligence is an option 
that should also be considered since in healthcare 
applications, the interpretability of machine learning 
models is of utmost importance. 
 
Finally, the development of a working application can 
be another goal, where the whole approach could be 
implemented as a fully operational solution on web and 
mobile platforms.

IV. EXPERIMENTAL SETUP 
The experiment has been formulated with an objective 
to assess the performance of different machine learning 
and deep learning algorithms in predicting heart diseases 
based on medical data. This part provides information 
on the dataset used, pre-processing, architecture of the 
model, training, and testing. 
 
A. Description of the Dataset 
 
The dataset utilized for this research work comprises 
structured clinical datasets acquired from publicly 
accessible medical databases. The dataset involves 
several patient records having characteristics related to 
the diagnosis of heart disease. 
 
The main features of the dataset are the age, gender, 
chest pain type, resting blood pressure, serum 
cholesterol, 
fasting 
blood 
sugar, 
resting 
electrocardiographic (ECG) test result, maximum heart 
rate obtained, exercise-induced angina, and many more. 
 
The dataset contains categorical and numeric attributes. 
The target attribute is an indicator of whether the 
patients have any heart disease or not. 
 
B. Data Preprocessing 
 
Data preprocessing is important for enhancing the 
performance and efficacy of the prediction models. 
Inconsistencies, missing data, and differences in scale 
among others may affect the accuracy of predictions. 
 
At the first step, missing values are treated appropriately 
through techniques such as using the mean or mode of a 
variable as an imputation method, depending on whether 
it is a categorical or numerical feature. Any duplicate 
values are eliminated. 
 
In case of categorical variables like chest pain type and 
ECG, label or one-hot encoding is used to convert 
categorical features to numeric ones. This enhances the 
interpretability by machine learning algorithms. 
 
Features are also scaled through appropriate methods 
such as Min-Max scaling or standardization, making 
them 
more 
comparable 
and 
improving 
their 
interpretation. 
 
The data is finally split into training and test sets, 
commonly with an 80% training and 20% testing ratio. 
 
C. Feature Engineering 
 
Feature engineering is employed to improve the quality 
of input data and the performance of the predictive 
models. Some of the approaches employed in this 
project include feature selection and transformation. 
 
Correlation analysis is used to find out the most 
important features that contribute to predicting heart 
disease. Unrelated features are filtered out, and highly 
correlated features are removed. 
 
Moreover, sophisticated algorithms such as Restricted 
Boltzmann Machine (RBM) can be employed to extract 
latent representations of the data. 
 
D. Model Configuration and Training 
 
Numerous machine learning and deep learning models 
have been trained on the dataset. 
 
Restricted Boltzman Machine,AdaBoost, and XGBoost 
are some of the machine learning models employed in 
the study. These models were chosen because they have 
proven to work effectively in classification problems. 
 
ANN and LSTM neural networks are also used for 
prediction. The Artificial Neural Network algorithm is 
made up of numerous hidden layers, each of which uses 
an activation function such as ReLU and Sigmoid. 
 
LSTM, on the other hand, captures long-term 
dependencies within the dataset despite its structured 
nature. 
 
Learning rate, the number of trees, tree depth, and 
hidden layers are tuned. 
 
E. Design of the Hybrid Model 
 
To further improve prediction accuracy, we design a 
hybrid model that combines deep learning and machine 
learning approaches. Specifically, our hybrid model 
consists of combining the power of LSTM with that of 
XGBoost. 
 
In our model, we use LSTM for feature extraction and 
apply the XGBoost classifier to do final classification. 
 
F. Performance Metrics 
 
The models are assessed based on various performance 
metrics to evaluate their performance comprehensively. 
 
Accuracy represents the performance of the model in 
terms of overall correctness of predictions. In addition 
to accuracy, precision and recall are used to measure 
how well the model predicts positive and negative cases. 
 
F1-score is a metric that balances between precision and 
recall of the model. ROC curve and AUC values can be 
calculated to measure classification performance. 
 
Confusion matrices provide an overview of model 
performance by illustrating TP, TN, FP, and FN values 
of the model.

V. Results and Discussion 
 
In this part, the performance evaluation of different 
types of machine learning and deep learning algorithms 
employed in heart disease prediction is discussed. The 
findings of this analysis are discussed in light of the 
evaluation metrics and comparisons to determine the 
most suitable model. 
 
A. Performance Evaluation of Models 
 
All machine learning algorithms and deep learning 
algorithms developed for this study were tested based on 
the test dataset. 
The findings suggest that conventional machine learning 
algorithms yield stable results, whereas deep learning 
algorithms exhibit better performance owing to their 
efficiency in capturing complex relationships between 
input variables. 
 
It is observed that among all developed models, Random 
Forest and XGBoost worked efficiently owing to their 
ensembling nature; however, deep learning models, i.e., 
ANN and LSTM, delivered better prediction accuracy.

C. Confusion Matrix Analysis 
 
Confusion matrices are utilized to assess the accuracy of 
the models. 
The proposed models exhibit high accuracy regarding 
true positives and negatives, which indicate the ability 
to classify the disease and absence correctly. 
Additionally, the number of false positives and false 
negatives is relatively low, which plays an essential role 
in medical diagnostics. 
 
It is crucial to minimize false negatives in heart disease 
prediction because neglecting a positive result may lead 
to severe health outcomes. 
 
D. ROC Curve and AUC Analysis 
The Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve 
analyzes the performance of a classifier at various 
threshold settings. 
 
The Area Under the Curve (AUC) results of the models 
show high classification performance levels. Advanced 
models like XGBoost and LSTM perform better than 
traditional classifiers as they have high AUC results, 
indicating their classification prowess.

classification prowess of XGBoost to minimize errors in 
classification.

F. Discussion 
Some of the key findings observed from the experiments 
are that machine learning models provide strong baseline 
performance for heart disease prediction, while deep 
learning models outperform traditional approaches by 
effectively learning complex patterns and relationships 
within medical data. Feature engineering significantly 
improves model accuracy by selecting and transforming 
important attributes, and hybrid models achieve the best 
results by combining the strengths of multiple algorithms. 
However, the overall performance of the models depends 
heavily on factors such as dataset size, feature quality, and 
preprocessing techniques, as insufficient or poor-quality 
data can reduce the generalization capability of deep 
learning models. The proposed system demonstrates high 
efficiency, reliability, and predictive capability, making it 
suitable for supporting early diagnosis and real-time 
clinical decision-making in heart disease detection. 
Furthermore, the system helps healthcare professionals 
make faster and more accurate treatment decisions, 
improving overall patient care outcomes.

VI. CONCLUSION 
This analysis evaluated both single and hybrid machine 
learning models for heart disease prediction using 
performance metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, 
F1-Score, and AUC. Among the individual models, Long 
Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Feedforward Neural 
Network (FNN), and Restricted Boltzmann Machine 
(RBM) showed better performance than models like 
XGBoost, CatBoost, MLP, and GRU. Based on these 
results, hybrid models were created by combining the best-
performing models. Among all hybrid models, the LSTM 
+ XGBoost model achieved the best results with high 
accuracy (0.81), precision (0.83), recall (0.82), and F1-
score (0.82). Its superior performance is due to the 
effective combination of deep learning and boosting 
techniques, which improves prediction accuracy and 
reduces errors. Compared to other hybrid models such as 
RBM + FNN, XGBoost + RBM, and LSTM + FNN, the 
LSTM + XGBoost model performed the best, showing that 
hybrid approaches are more effective for heart disease 
prediction. 
 
VII. Future Scope 
Despite the success of the proposed system in yielding 
positive results, there are some directions for future 
research and development. 
 
For instance, the future development of this model could 
involve the use of extensive and heterogeneous real-
world datasets, which will increase the robustness and 
flexibility of the model. Furthermore, by adding, 

1 
 
genetics, and medical history will make the model even 
more accurate. 
 
Another area for improvement is to use IoT devices and 
wearable technology, which will enable real-time data 
acquisition, thus allowing us to perform real-time 
prediction of patients' health condition. 
 
Using state-of-the-art machine learning approaches, like 
CNNs or transformers, can result in better outcomes. 
The use of explainable artificial intelligence is an option 
that should also be considered since in healthcare 
applications, the interpretability of machine learning 
models is of utmost importance. 
 
Finally, the development of a working application can 
be another goal, where the whole approach could be 
implemented as a fully operational solution on web and 
mobile platforms.
